name: Mythos 5 Partial US Release — Day 15

name: Claude Code v2.1.195 — Week 26 Recap
hook: `claude mcp login <n>` / `claude mcp logout <n>` authenticate MCP servers from the shell without touching the /mcp menu. `/rewind` can now jump back past a `/clear`. Shell mode explains command output (no second prompt). Background subagents surface permission prompts in the main session instead of auto-denying. June 27 patch also cuts streaming CPU ~37% and fixes hook matchers on hyphenated names.
recurring_note: ↑ Day 3 — Week 26 (v2.1.185–v2.1.195); biggest batch: MCP auth CLI, /rewind cross-clear, background agent UX

name: claude-howto

name: Claude Agent in JetBrains IDEs (GitHub Copilot)
hook: As of June 22, GitHub Copilot supports Claude as an agent provider in JetBrains IDEs (public preview). Install the Claude Code CLI, point JetBrains at it in settings, select 'Claude' in the Copilot Chat panel — full agentic file editing and tool use from within IntelliJ, PyCharm, WebStorm, etc. Configurable permissions coming; currently bypass mode.

name: Bumblebee (Perplexity AI)
hook: 4.6k stars — Perplexity's read-only supply-chain scanner for developer tools. Reads ~/.claude.json, .mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json, and 6 other MCP config paths, flags matches against maintained threat-intel catalogs (updated via PRs as new campaigns emerge). Zero non-stdlib deps, single Go binary, v0.1.2 (June 18).

name: Claude SEO Plugin
hook: 10k stars, MIT — 25 sub-skills and 18 sub-agents covering technical SEO, E-E-A-T, schema/GEO/AEO, backlinks, local SEO, e-commerce, international SEO, and Google APIs, plus PDF/Excel reporting. Supports SPA headless rendering. v2.2.0 (June 12).

name: MCP OAuth Token Hijack (Mitiga Labs)
hook: Mitiga Labs documented a 5-step MITM chain: a malicious npm postinstall hook silently edits ~/.claude.json to redirect all MCP traffic through attacker infrastructure, harvesting plaintext OAuth bearer tokens (persistent, broadly scoped, unattributable server-side). Reported to Anthropic April 10; Anthropic declined to patch, citing user consent as a prerequisite. Security Boulevard and SecurityWeek picked it up in June.

Ships an MCP server for in-session use.
